speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand the severity and cause, can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if the pain is localized to one spot or spread out?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Lyme Arthritis/Cellulitis)

The patient's recent camping trip in Minnesota, self-resolving knee pain, and current wrist pain with fever and skin lesions are highly suggestive of a tick-borne illness. REQUEST TEST: Lyme serology (ELISA and Western Blot). REQUEST IMAGES: Photos of the wrist lesions and knee to check for erythema migrans or septic arthritis signs.
